title: After hitting a pothole or curb
h1: I hit a pothole or curb. Is my car damaged?
metaDesc: Hit a pothole or curb? What to check right away, which signs mean pull over, and what a shop looks at: tires, wheels, alignment and suspension.
synonyms: steering wheel crooked after hitting curb
intro: A hard hit from a pothole, curb or debris can damage a tire, a wheel or the steering. Some damage shows right away and some shows later. These questions help you decide what to do now.
safety: If a tire is losing air fast, has a bulge, or the wheel looks bent or cracked, don't drive on it. Put on the spare or call for help.
If the steering wheel is suddenly crooked, the car pulls hard, or you hear grinding or scraping, pull over when it's safe.
If you smell fuel or see fluid leaking after the hit, turn off the engine and step away from the car.
If a red brake warning light came on after the hit, stop and don't drive until it's checked.

q_now.q: After the hit, what do you notice?

opts.a: A tire is going flat, or has a bulge or cut on the side
Fluid is dripping, or I smell fuel
The steering wheel shakes, sits crooked, or the car pulls
A new clunk, rattle or scraping noise
Strong shaking or a hard pull, and it's hard to keep straight
Mild: the wheel is a little off-center, or a light shake at some speeds
Tire pressure light (looks like a horseshoe with !)
Another light, or I'm not sure

result.title: The tire is damaged. Don't drive on it
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe, away from traffic. Put on the spare if you can do it safely, or call roadside assistance.
if: If the wheel looks bent or cracked, tell the tire shop. A new tire won't seal on a damaged wheel.
If you're in a traffic lane or someone is hurt, call 911.
result.why: A hard hit can pinch the tire against the wheel, cutting it from the inside. A bulge means the inner layers are broken, and the tire can burst without warning.

causes.name: Tire pinched against the wheel
causes.clues: A bulge or cut on the sidewall.

causes.name: Bent wheel letting air out
causes.clues: The tire loses air slowly and the wheel edge looks dented.

result.title: A leak after a hit needs checking before you drive
result.now: Turn the engine off and step away from the car if you smell fuel. Don't drive it. Have it towed or have a mechanic come to you.
if: If there's smoke or a strong fuel smell, keep everyone away and call 911.
If the temperature gauge rises or a red light comes on, don't restart the engine.
result.why: Debris or a hard hit can crack the oil pan, a fuel line, a radiator or a brake line. Driving with these leaks can damage the engine, start a fire, or affect the brakes.

causes.name: Cracked oil pan
causes.clues: Dark brown or black drips under the engine.

causes.name: Damaged radiator or coolant hose
causes.clues: Green, orange or pink fluid; a sweet smell.

causes.name: Damaged fuel or brake line
causes.clues: A fuel smell, or clear-to-brown fluid near a wheel.

result.title: A wheel, tire or steering part may be bent
result.now: Pull over when it's safe. Don't drive it if it's hard to keep straight. Have it towed or have a mechanic come to you.
if: If you can see the wheel leaning in or out, or the tire rubbing, don't move the car.
result.why: A hard hit can bend a wheel, a steering link or a suspension arm. Strong shaking or a hard pull means the car may not steer or stop as it should.

causes.name: Bent wheel
causes.clues: Shaking that gets worse with speed.

causes.name: Bent steering or suspension part
causes.clues: The steering wheel sits crooked and the car pulls.

causes.name: Damaged tire
causes.clues: A bulge or flat spot.

result.title: The alignment may be knocked out, or a wheel slightly bent
result.now: Get the alignment and wheels checked within a few days. Drive gently until then.
if: If the pull or shake gets worse, or you hear clunking, stop driving it and have it checked.
If a tire starts losing air, check the pressure and look for a bulge.
result.why: Even a mild hit can shift the alignment or bend a wheel slightly. Left alone, it can wear out tires early and make the car harder to control in an emergency.

causes.name: Alignment knocked out
causes.clues: The steering wheel sits a bit crooked.

causes.name: Slightly bent wheel
causes.clues: A shake at certain speeds.

causes.name: Wheel weight knocked off
causes.clues: A new vibration at highway speed.

you: Look at the tire sidewall for bulges.

result.title: A tire may be losing air
result.now: At the next safe stop, check all four tires with a pressure gauge and look for bulges or cuts. Fill to the pressure on the driver's door sticker.
if: If a tire is very low, flat or has a bulge, don't drive on it. Put on the spare or call for help.
If it goes low again within a day, have it checked right away.
result.why: A hit can damage a tire or bend a wheel so air leaks out slowly. The tire pressure light warns you before the tire goes flat.

causes.name: Slow leak from tire damage
causes.clues: One tire is lower than the others.

causes.name: Bent wheel edge
causes.clues: A dent on the wheel rim.

causes.name: Damaged tire pressure sensor
causes.clues: All tires are at the right pressure, but the light stays on.

result.title: A red brake light after a hit can mean a damaged brake line
result.now: Pull over when it's safe and don't drive it. Have it towed or have a mechanic come to you.
if: If the brake pedal feels soft or goes down further than usual, don't try to move the car.
If the parking brake is on, release it and see if the light goes off. If it stays on, don't drive.
result.why: The red brake light can mean low brake fluid. A hit can damage a brake line or hose, and fluid can leak out, which makes the brakes weaker.

causes.name: Damaged brake line or hose
causes.clues: Wet fluid near a wheel.

causes.name: Low brake fluid
causes.clues: The fluid level is below the MIN mark.

causes.name: Parking brake on
causes.clues: The light goes off when the parking brake is released.

result.title: A wheel speed sensor or its wire may have been damaged
result.now: Get it checked within a few days. Normal brakes usually still work, but anti-lock brakes (ABS) and traction control may not. Leave extra stopping room, especially in rain or snow.
if: If the red brake light comes on too, or the pedal feels different, stop and don't drive.
result.why: Each wheel has a speed sensor with a wire that runs near the suspension. A hit can damage the sensor or pull the wire loose, which turns off ABS and traction control.

causes.name: Damaged wheel speed sensor or wire
causes.clues: The light came on right after the hit.

causes.name: Damaged wheel bearing
causes.clues: A new hum or grinding from one wheel.

you: Look at the wires near each wheel for anything hanging.

result.title: A part may have been damaged or knocked loose
result.now: At a safe stop, look under the car for anything hanging or dragging. Get it checked within a few days.
if: If something is dragging on the ground, don't drive it. It can catch and come loose.
If the noise comes with a pull, shake or loose steering, stop and have it checked.
result.why: A hard hit can bend or loosen a heat shield, the exhaust, a plastic underbody cover or a suspension part. Some are harmless, and some affect steering.

causes.name: Loose heat shield or underbody cover
causes.clues: A rattle or scraping at certain speeds.

causes.name: Damaged exhaust
causes.clues: The car sounds louder.

causes.name: Damaged suspension or steering part
causes.clues: A clunk over bumps, or the car handles differently.

you: Look under the car for hanging parts (engine off, on level ground).

result.title: Probably fine, but watch for signs over the next few days
result.now: Look at the tire that hit for bulges, cuts or a bent wheel. Check the tire pressures in the next day or two. Book a check if anything changes.
if: If the car starts pulling, the steering wheel sits crooked, or a new shake or noise starts, get it checked.
If a bulge appears on the tire later, don't drive on it.
result.why: Many hits cause no damage. Some damage, like a slow leak, a small bulge or an alignment change, can take a few days to show.

causes.name: No damage
causes.clues: Everything feels the same.

causes.name: Small tire or wheel damage that shows later
causes.clues: A bulge or slow leak in the next days.

causes.name: Alignment change
causes.clues: Uneven tire wear or a slight pull later.

you: Look at the tire and wheel.

result.title: Check the tires, then have the car looked at
result.now: At a safe stop, look at the tires and wheels for bulges, cuts or dents, and check for leaks under the car. Get it inspected within a few days.
if: If you find a bulge, a flat or a bent wheel, don't drive on it.
If a red warning light is on, pull over and stop.
result.why: Not every problem is obvious right after a hit. A quick look plus a shop check catches most damage early.

causes.name: Tire or wheel damage
causes.clues: A bulge, cut or dent.

causes.name: Alignment change
causes.clues: A slight pull.

you: Look at the tires and wheels.
